Order 
1.

This is applicant's first application under Section 482 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Section 438 of Criminal Procedure Code, 1973) for grant of anticipatory bail, as he/she is apprehending his/her arrest in connection with Crime No.0345/2024 registered at Police Station Neemuch City, District Neemuch (MP) for offence punishable under Section 120-B, 419, 420, 447,
467, 468 and 471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

entities.text: Police Station Neemuch City, District Neemuch
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. Allegations against the applicant is of fraud.

It is alleged that the applicant entered into an agreement to sale of the disputed land admeasuring 46.46 sq. mtr. with co-accused Balwant Singh on 29/10/2020 and on the basis of the said agreement, the co-accused Balwant Singh sold the land through a registered sale deed to one Bhuralal on 29/05/2020, however, subsequently it was found that the land belong to the government.

3. Counsel for the applicant has submitted that the co-accused Balwant NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:205 2 MCRC-53225-2025 Singh has already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.55789/2025 on 08/12/2025 and the case of the applicant is on better footing as the applicant has also been given a certificate by Gram Panchayat, Barkhedi Panedi that the applicant is in possession of the said land since last 40 years.

Counsel has also submitted that Prabhudas Bairagi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105044496/
1 the land was also mutated in the name of co-accused Balwant Singh, who has been granted bail as aforesaid.

entities.text: Prabhudas Bairagi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, it is submitted that the custodial interrogation of the applicant would not be necessary.
Hence, it is submitted that the application be allowed and the applicant be released on anticipatory bail.
4. Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer and it is submitted that no case for anticipatory bail is made out.

5. On due consideration of the rival submissions and perusal of the case diary as also the order passed by this Court in the case of Balwant Singh on 08/12/2025 (supra), although it is found that it is wrongly mentioned in the said order that Balwant Singh purchased the disputed land through registered sale deed, although, he had entered into an agreement to sale with the seller/present applicant Prabhudas Bairagi, however, it is also found that the name of Balwant Singh was also mutated in the revenue records.

In such circumstances, since the disputed facts are involved in the case and the applicant is said to have been in possession of the land since last 40 years, this Court is of the considered opinion that the custodial interrogation of the applicant is not necessary in the present case.
In view of the same, applicant has made out a case for grant of anticipatory bail.
6. Accordingly, this application is allowed.

It is directed that in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:205 3 MCRC-53225-2025 event of arrest, applicant shall be released on bail,
upon his/her executing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand only) and furnishing one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
7. The applicant shall make himself/herself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
He/she shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Certified copy as per rules.
